chunks: Wuhayb ibn Hafs narrated from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made his slave mudabbar while he was in debt, fleeing from the debt. He عليه السلام said: “There is no tadbir for him; but if he made him mudabbar in a state of health and well-being, then the creditors have no claim over him.”

key_terms.تَدْبِيرَ: the legal act of conditional emancipation upon death
key_terms.دَبَّرَ: declared delayed emancipation of a slave to take effect after the owner's death
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: an outstanding debt owed by the person
key_terms.فِرَارًا: as an act of fleeing or evasion
key_terms.لِلدُّيَّانِ: for the creditors; those owed debts

ai.seo_question: Is tadbir valid if a debtor declares his slave freed after death in order to escape paying debts?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tadbir when a person is indebted. If delayed emancipation is declared as a means of evading creditors, it is invalid; but if it was established in a sound state without such evasive intent, creditors cannot seize the slave.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3466 - Wuhayb ibn Hafs narrated from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about a man who made his slave mudabbar (to be freed after his death) while he was in debt, intending to escape from paying the debt.
Imam (as) said: "There is no valid tadbir (declaration of delayed emancipation) in this case. However, if he made the tadbir while he was in good health and free from any financial distress, then the creditors have no claim over the slave."
